stats.title: Statistics
stats.windowSummary: Last {days, number} days · {sessions, number} finished workouts
stats.empty: No finished workouts in the last {days, number} days. Statistics start once a workout is finished — an open one is still being written.
stats.volumeSummary: Tonnage over working weight × reps sets, by week
stats.volumeNote: Working sets only, and weight × reps only. Bodyweight and timed work is real training that produces no tonnage, so none of it is in this figure.
stats.loadSummary: Foster session-RPE load — session RPE times duration — by week
stats.loadNote: Session RPE × duration, in arbitrary units. A week with no bar is a week whose load is unknown, not a week of no training.
stats.loadUnknown: {n, number} of {total, number} workouts in the last {days, number} days recorded no session RPE or no finish time. Their load is unknown, not zero, so they are left out.
stats.loadNoneKnown: None of the {n, number} workouts in the last {days, number} days recorded both a session RPE and a finish time, so there is no load to sum.
stats.musclesTitle: Hard sets per muscle, last {days, number} days
stats.musclesSummary: Hard sets credited to each muscle over the last {days, number} days
stats.musclesEmpty: No working sets in the last {days, number} days.
stats.bandLegend: The shaded band is {low, number}–{high, number} hard sets a week, the range commonly cited for hypertrophy (Schoenfeld).
stats.secondaryCreditNote: A working set credits 1 to its primary muscle and {credit, number} to each secondary one. That {credit, number} is a convention this project chose, not a constant of nature — published guidelines count sets differently, so these totals sit beside the band rather than being measured by it.
stats.acwrContext: {acute, number} AU over {acuteDays, number} days against {chronic, number} AU over {chronicDays, number}
stats.acwrBandLegend: The shaded band is {low, number}–{high, number}, the range commonly cited; the hairline marks {elevated, number}, above which the ratio is usually called elevated.
stats.acwrCaveat: This ratio has been substantially criticised on statistical grounds. The 7-day window sits inside the 28-day one, so the two are autocorrelated by construction, and the reported sweet spot does not survive reanalysis once that artifact and the coupling of a ratio to its own denominator are controlled (Impellizzeri et al.). Read it as a prompt to look again at a week far out of line with the month behind it — never as a diagnosis.
stats.acwrNeedsSessions: Needs {min, number} workouts with both a session RPE and a finish time in the last {days, number} days. {known, number} so far.
stats.acwrNeedsSessionsPartial: Needs {min, number} workouts with both a session RPE and a finish time in the last {days, number} days. {known, number} so far, and {unknown, number} more are missing one of the two.
stats.acwrNoLoad: Every workout in the last {days, number} days summed to zero load, so there is no ratio to take.
stats.progressionEmpty: No weight × reps exercise was trained in this window, so there is no one-rep-max estimate to plot.
stats.progressionMore: {n, number} more exercises have an estimate and are not drawn here. Open one from the catalogue.
stats.e1rmChartSummary: Best reliable estimated one-rep max per training day for {name}
stats.recordsLegend: Ringed points beat everything before them in this window: {days}.
stats.noRecordsInWindow: No session in this window beat every one before it.
stats.unreliableSkipped: {n, number} sessions produced estimates only from sets above {reps, number} reps, where Epley stops being reliable. They are not plotted and cannot set a record.
stats.unreliableOnly: Trained {n, number} times in this window, but every working set was above {reps, number} reps, where the Epley estimate stops being reliable. Nothing is plotted, and none of it can set a record.
stats.noEstimates: No working set in this window carried both a weight and a rep count, so there is no estimate to plot.
stats.slopeValue: {value, number} kg per session, over the last {n, number}
stats.slopeFlat: Flat over the last {n, number} sessions
stats.slopeUnavailable: Needs {min, number} sessions with a reliable estimate before a trend means anything. {n, number} so far.

correlation.title: Sleep and training
correlation.empty: Nothing logged yet in the last {days, number} days.
correlation.caveatTitle: What this is, and what it is not
correlation.caveat: This is a correlation within one person’s data — yours — and a correlation is not causation. Nothing here was controlled or randomised. A hard session can shorten the night that follows as easily as a short night can soften the day after it, and both move with the day of the week, which none of these measures adjusts for: a weekend is a longer night and a different session at the same time. Read a coefficient as a question worth asking, never as an effect.
correlation.noPvalue: There is deliberately no significance test. Self-selected, unblinded, opportunistically collected data from one person cannot support one, and its only practical effect would be to license reading noise as a finding. The number of days behind each coefficient is printed instead.
correlation.pairedDays: {n, number} days with both a logged night and a finished workout
correlation.sleepOnlyDays: {n, number} nights logged with no workout that day
correlation.sessionOnlyDays: {n, number} workouts on a night that was never logged — there is no predictor for those, so they enter none of the measures below
correlation.method: Spearman’s ρ on ranks, so one 14-hour catch-up night cannot drag a coefficient and no straight-line relationship is assumed. The night before a workout on a given day is that day’s sleep record: a sleep is keyed to the day it ended and a workout to the day it started, which is what makes the two a single-column join.
correlation.axisLegend: Horizontal: sleep, {xLow} on the left to {xHigh} on the right. Vertical: {yLow} at the bottom to {yHigh} at the top.
correlation.volumeDescription: Minutes asleep against the tonnage of the working sets that followed, over the days that trained. A rest day is excluded rather than counted as zero tonnage — not training is not a session that produced nothing.
correlation.volumeChartSummary: Each day with both a logged night and a finished workout: minutes asleep, and the tonnage that followed
correlation.volumeNotEnough: {n, number} of {min, number} paired days. Nothing is drawn below that: under about twenty points a rank correlation is decided by the handful of days at the ends of the ranking, and one week of illness moves it across the whole range.
correlation.volumeNoVariance: {n, number} paired days, but every one of them has the same sleep length, or the same tonnage. There is no ranking to correlate.
correlation.rpeDescription: Minutes asleep against the mean RPE of the working sets that followed. The set-level mean rather than the session RPE, because it is recorded while training rather than as one impression afterwards, and it comes off the same sets the tonnage does.
correlation.rpeChartSummary: Each day with a logged night and at least one working set that recorded an RPE
correlation.rpeNotEnough: {n, number} of {min, number} paired days recorded an RPE on a working set. Volume can answer while this one cannot: a session logged without any RPE still has a tonnage.
correlation.rpeNoVariance: {n, number} paired days, but every one of them has the same sleep length, or the same mean RPE. There is no ranking to correlate.
correlation.trainedTitle: Sleep against whether you trained at all
correlation.trainedDescription: Minutes asleep against whether a session happened, over every logged night — the one measure where a rest day is an observation rather than a gap. No chart: the outcome has two values, and a scatter of two rows says less than the number does.
correlation.trainedNoVariance: {n, number} logged nights, but you trained on every one of them, or on none of them. There is nothing to rank.

maintenance.intro: Whole-vault jobs. Each runs in batches in the background, reports real progress, and can be stopped at any point — everything already processed stays processed.

pastedFormatting.title: Clear formatting that came in from a paste
pastedFormatting.description: Rewrites every note, removing text colour, highlight colour, column widths copied from a source table, and link styling carried in from another page. Everything that means something is kept: tables, header rows, merged cells, lists, links and where they point, code blocks, headings, bold, italic and strikethrough.
pastedFormatting.warning: This cannot be undone. A colour you chose yourself is stored exactly like a colour that arrived with a paste, so this removes both, in every note. Nothing can tell them apart after the fact, and there is no way to put them back — export anything you care about first.
